Psychoacoustic and Signal Processing Foundations

items: Interaural Time & Level Differences (ITD/ILD): Duplex theory dictates which horizontal localization relies on sub-700-microsecond ear arrival time deltas at low frequencies and head-shadow amplitude attenuation above 1.5 kHz.

Spatial Aliasing Frequencies: Loudspeaker driver spacing strictly determines the upper cutoff frequency where discrete sound arrays dissolve into destructive spatial interference lobes.

Spherical Harmonics and Higher-Order Ambisonics (HOA): Encoding directional 3D audio fields into orthogonal spherical harmonic expansion coefficients decouples sound design from specific physical loudspeaker layouts.

body.text: Personalized HRTF Pinna Scanning via Computer Vision

Generic HRTF profiles often cause headphone listeners to experience front-back confusion or perceive sound sources as collapsing inside their skull. Modern binaural engines employ machine learning models to synthesize custom HRTF filter kernels directly from smartphone photos of a user ear pinna, unlocking true externalized 3D spatial clarity.
